2027-05-09.title: Sixth Sunday after Qyomtho
readings: I am the Lord; I will free you
Your immortal spirit is in all things
I have swept away your sins like a cloud
The eyes of your heart enlightened
It is to your advantage that I go away
2027-05-09.alt: Sunday between the Ascension and Pentecost. In the 2025–26 lectionary this was Social Communication Media Day. Remind the faithful about Pentecost next Sunday.
2027-05-09.verse: It is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.
theo: Between the Ascension and Pentecost the Church lives in the upper room. The apostles, “together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus”, are “constantly devoting themselves to prayer.” Jesus has gone to the Father; the Spirit has not yet come. It is a time of waiting, but not of emptiness: it is the Church at prayer, gathered around Mary.

Jesus had told them: “It is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.” His physical presence was limited to one place; the Spirit will make him present everywhere, in every heart and every altar. The Spirit “will prove the world wrong about sin and righteousness and judgment”: he convicts, converts and gives courage.

In the evening Gospel we hear the beginning of Jesus' great priestly prayer: “Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son so that the Son may glorify you… And this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.” The ascended Christ continues this prayer for us at the Father's right hand.

God says to Joshua as he takes up Moses' task: “Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.” St Paul prays that “with the eyes of your heart enlightened, you may know what is the hope to which he has called you.” Let us spend this week like the apostles: in prayer, with Mary, waiting for the Spirit.
conn: The room of the Last Supper becomes the room of waiting and of Pentecost (Acts 1:13; 2:1).
Mary, overshadowed by the Spirit at the Annunciation, prays with the Church for the Spirit's coming (Acts 1:14).
As Joshua received Moses' charge, the apostles receive Christ's mission; the same promise: “I will be with you.”
Isaiah 44:22: the forgiveness the Spirit brings when he convicts the world of sin.
altar: At every Holy Qurbono the Church does what the apostles did in the upper room: gathered with Mary and the saints, she prays for the Spirit, and the Spirit comes upon the gifts and upon us.
outline: The Spirit makes Christ present everywhere.
The Church at prayer with Mary.
Point 4 · Eternal life is to know God
live: Pray each day until Pentecost for one gift of the Holy Spirit.
Pray the Rosary this week with the intention of a new Pentecost in your family.
Share something good and true online this week; avoid sharing gossip or anger.
fathers: It was expedient for them that the form of a servant be taken from their sight, so that, no longer clinging to the flesh, they might love him spiritually and receive the Spirit (Tractates on John 94).
Christ had to depart in the flesh so that the Spirit might dwell in us; through the Spirit Christ himself is with us (Commentary on John 10).
magis: Only when the hour of his glorification had come did Jesus promise the coming of the Spirit; the Spirit will be with us for ever.
Mary, filled with the Holy Spirit, is present with the apostles at the dawn of the last times.
The Church sees the means of social communication as gifts of God to be used for the good.
saints: The days of prayer for the Holy Spirit continue. Sunday 16 May: Pentecost.
2027-05-09.prayer: Lord Jesus, you went to the Father so that the Advocate might come. Gather us with Mary and the apostles in prayer, make us strong and courageous, enlighten the eyes of our hearts, and send your Holy Spirit upon your Church. Amen.

quick: “It is to your advantage that I go away”: the Spirit will make Christ present everywhere.
The Church waits in prayer with Mary.
“Be strong and courageous; the Lord is with you.”
2027-05-09.action: Pray each day until Pentecost for one gift of the Holy Spirit.
2027-05-09.question: Which gift of the Holy Spirit do I most need?
2027-05-09.special: Sixth Sunday after Qyomtho. Announce Pentecost next Sunday. (In 2025–26 also Social Communication Media Day; check the collection.)
illus: Before a big family wedding in Kerala, relatives gather in the house days earlier to pray the Rosary each evening. The house becomes an upper room. That is what the Church does between the Ascension and Pentecost.

family.explain: After Jesus went to heaven, his friends prayed together with Mary, waiting for the Holy Spirit Jesus had promised.
family.intention: We pray for the gifts of the Holy Spirit for each of us.
family.ask: Ask: “Which gift of the Spirit do we need most in our family?”

catechism: The gifts of the Holy Spirit.
kidsaint: After Jesus went to heaven, Mary prayed with the apostles, waiting for the Holy Spirit. She is the Mother of the Church. Lesson: pray with Mary, and the Spirit will come.
term: In the 2025–26 lectionary the Sixth Sunday after Qyomtho was Social Communication Media Day, when the Church prays for the right use of the media.
termMore: John 17, the prayer of Jesus to the Father at the Last Supper, is called his “high-priestly prayer”: for his glory, for his disciples, and for all who will believe.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, we are living the days between the Ascension and Pentecost. Jesus has gone to the Father; the Spirit has not yet come. And what did the apostles do? They went to the upper room and “devoted themselves to prayer, together with Mary the mother of Jesus.”

Jesus had said something surprising: “It is to your advantage that I go away.” How can it be better that Jesus goes? Because when he was on earth he could be in one place at a time. The Spirit makes him present everywhere: in every heart, in every family, on every altar. The Spirit will convict the world of sin, of righteousness and of judgment.

In the evening Gospel Jesus prays: “Father, the hour has come… This is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.” He is still praying for us at the right hand of the Father.

And God says to us what he said to Joshua: “Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.” This week let us do what the apostles did: pray with Mary, every day, “Come, Holy Spirit.” Amen.
kids: Children, after Jesus went back to heaven, his friends waited in a room in Jerusalem. What were they doing? Praying, together with Mary!
Jesus had promised to send the Holy Spirit to help them. Next Sunday we will celebrate when the Spirit came!
This week, let's pray with Mary every day: “Come, Holy Spirit!”

intro: Theme: “Waiting for the Spirit with Mary.”

Between the Ascension and Pentecost the Church waits in the upper room. Jesus has said it is better for us that he goes, for then the Advocate will come. His high-priestly prayer asks that we may all be one.

sub: The apostles, with Mary and the women, devote themselves to prayer.
Waiting is not idleness; it is opening the heart to God's gift.
God's spirit already fills all things; we pray that he fill us anew.
q: For your immortal spirit is in all things.
All these were constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus, as well as his brothers.
points.apply: Pray the Rosary each day this week for a new Pentecost in your family.

points.h: Better for you that I go
sub: Jesus' bodily presence was in one place; the Spirit makes him present everywhere.
The Spirit convicts the world of sin, not to condemn but to heal.
Isaiah: God sweeps away our sins like mist and calls us back.
q: I have swept away your transgressions like a cloud, and your sins like mist; return to me, for I have redeemed you.
It is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.
points.apply: Ask the Holy Spirit to show you one sin to be healed, and confess it.

points.h: That they may all be one
sub: God promised: “I will take you as my people, and I will be your God.”
Jesus prays that his disciples be one as he and the Father are one.
Unity in families, parishes and among Christians is the Spirit's work and our task.
q: I will take you as my people, and I will be your God.
That they may all be one. As you, Father, are in me and I am in you, may they also be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me.
points.apply: Heal one division before Pentecost: call, visit or forgive.

concl: The upper room teaches us to wait, pray and seek unity.
Let us prepare with Mary for the coming of the Spirit next Sunday.
2027-05-09.resolve: Pray daily until Pentecost: “Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful.”
